newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end firmer ahead of Canada Day.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end firmer ahead of Canada Day.

text.p: Toronto's key stock index finished firmer in extremely thin trade on Monday, unfazed by weaker bonds while a skeleton crew of players staffed desks ahead of Tuesday's public and market holiday.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index added 11.34 points to reach 6437.74.
Only 44.1 million shares were traded at C$725.5 million ($525.7 million) shares, roughly half Toronto's daily amount.
The nation celebrates Canada Day on Tuesday.
"We're holding onto very modest gains while bonds and bills sold off today," said MMS International analyst Katherine Beattie. "But you can't read too much into it because volumes are low."

The few investors playing attention also ignored New York's frantic trading as it see-sawed to a positive close after unexpectedly strong U.S. new home sales. Sales rebounded by 7.1 percent in May after a revised 8.1 percent drop in April.
The information raised the specter of an interest rate hike following the U.S. Federal Reserve's two-day rate policy meeting which is scheduled to start on Tuesday.
Toronto's 14 sectors were evenly split between winners and losers by day's end. Consumer products, oils and pipelines firmed while real estate, media and conglomerates softened.
Advancing issues outnumbered 519 to 382 and 275 ended flat.
Canada's largest equities market ended the second quarter about 598 points or more than 10 percent higher than its opening level of 5840 points on April 1.

Amid hot issues, Crystallex International Inc. shares rose 0.30 to 7.00 in heavy dealings. The company said on Friday that senior Venezuelan officials had tried to promote a deal between the junior miner and Placer Dome Inc. to resolve an ownership controversy over the gold-rich Las Cristinas property.
